t: This is the Strand, a major street running just over three quarters of a mile from Trafalgar Square east to Temple Bar, where it becomes Fleet Street. It is part of the West End's theatreland. Several people have lived and died along it. In 1600 the Moroccan ambassador Abd el-Ouahed ben Messaoud lived here, sent to Queen Elizabeth's court to promote an alliance. Mildred Cooke, the translator and wife of Lord Burghley, died here. William Reynolds, the first private to receive the Victoria Cross, also died on the Strand. Sir George Barham, founder of Express Dairies, was born here.
